title: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
capsule: The Grand Duchy of Tuscany was an Italian state whose Medici foundation (1569) was replaced by the House of Habsburg-Lorraine in 1737 after the male Medici line died out with Gian Gastone. Suppressed by France and reorganized as the Etrurian Kingdom (1801–1807) and then annexed to the French Empire, it was restored to the Habsburg-Lorraine dynasty by the Congress of Vienna in 1814–1815 under Ferdinand III and then Leopold II. Leopold II granted a constitution in 1848 but Austrian intervention in 1849 and subsequent repression ended this experiment; popular uprising in 1859 drove Leopold II from Florence and Tuscany was annexed to the Kingdom of Sardinia in 1860, becoming part of unified Italy. The dataset window 1797–1849 covers the Napoleonic encroachment through the first revolutionary rupture.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are well defined by treaty and administrative record for the Habsburg-Lorraine period; the attestation window 1797–1849 is historically precise but encompasses discontinuous political regimes.
